notes.text: Ultimately, each person who has entered into the covenant of peace in the temple, which is a covenant with Christ, to be modeled like him, becomes the Tree of Life. Therefore in the temple, you are allowed to take root and grow and bring forth fruit, and these are the ones who fill the earth, therefore Eden is not just filled, or paradisiacal glory, it's not just filled with fruitful and productive trees, but it is filled with Israel, who is now fruitful and productive, having posterity as numerous as sand upon the seashore, or the stars in heaven, if you could count them, and they are now like the trees of Eden also. The only ones who can rise and live in the millennium and endure on into is the celestial kingdom, are those who have made the covenant of peace in the place where you make the peace, then they are the ones who take root and begin to grow and to fill the earth as Eden. Symbolically speaking, Alma was right on target in Alma Chapter 32, when he had you plant a seed and had that seed grow up and when it was finished, remember it was the tree of life.

quotes.text: Jacob will take root. The vineyard (Jacob) will take root, or will become firmly established, in the promised land; after the vineyard matures (blossoms and buds), it will fill "the world with fruit," which may speak of literal offspring (2 Ne. 3:4; Gen. 30:2) or possibly righteous deeds (Jer. 17:7-8).
quotes.speaker: Donald W. Parry
